title: Why Five Kingdoms, Not Two? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Curd bacteria, a green cell in pond water, bread mould, a mango tree and a cat: two kingdoms could not hold them all. Diya sorted them into five boxes with her own questions, then found that R. H. Whittaker had done the same in 1969. His five kingdoms are still the ones in your NCERT book.

You will see Whittaker's five main criteria, then watch the two old boxes break into Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia as bacteria, fungi, Chlamydomonas, Chlorella, Amoeba and Paramoecium move to their new kingdoms. Then we build Whittaker's comparison table (NCERT Table 2.1) live, one row at a time: cell type, cell wall, nuclear membrane, body organisation and mode of nutrition. A side-by-side of Monera and Protista, a pause-and-think check, a worked sort of six living things, the exam trap about single celled organisms, an original NEET pattern match-the-following question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 12 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
